description: CRITICAL FINDING: LM Studio silently routes multiple model IDs to the same loaded model. The preflight passes for voyage-4-nano and jina-v5-small were testing Qwen 0.6B, not their own models.
finding: When text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b is loaded, requests for voyage-4-nano and jina-embeddings-v5-text-small-retrieval are silently served by Qwen 0.6B. The response's model field confirms this: all three return model='text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b'. The embeddings are byte-identical (max_abs_diff = 0.00e+00).

evidence.test: Identical input text ('The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.') embedded via 4 model IDs

cross_model_similarity.qwen_vs_minilm: DIFFERENT (384d vs 1024d forces different model load)

impact_on_preflight.voyage_4_nano_preflight: INVALID — was testing Qwen 0.6B, not voyage-4-nano
impact_on_preflight.jina_v5_small_preflight: INVALID — was testing Qwen 0.6B, not jina-v5-small
impact_on_preflight.qwen_0_6b_preflight: VALID — confirmed stable, deterministic, correct model identity

impact_on_sprint.candidate_C_status: DEAD. BGE-M3 crashes. Voyage-4-nano and Jina-v5-small cannot be independently evaluated on this host because LM Studio routes them to Qwen. There is no operationally viable materially-different embedding model on this host.
options: A. Run a two-way sprint: lexical (A) vs Qwen hybrid (B). This is the only scientifically valid comparison available on this host.
B. Obtain a different host/provider that correctly serves voyage-4-nano or another materially different model.
C. Accept that the architecture decision cannot be made with a three-way comparison on this host.

root_cause: LM Studio's model loading mechanism appears to serve whichever 1024d model is currently in memory, regardless of the requested model ID. This is likely a GGUF/model-name resolution issue where LM Studio falls back to the loaded model when the requested model fails to load (or loads identically). This is a host-environment defect, not a model-quality defect.
